claims.text: In tungsten-based plasma-facing materials, high-temperature plastic strain is governed by the effectiveness of nanoscale oxide dispersions at grain boundaries.
In tungsten-based plasma-facing materials, high-temperature toughness is governed by the effectiveness of nanoscale oxide dispersions at grain boundaries.
Nanoscale oxide dispersions at grain boundaries pin dislocations.
Nanoscale oxide dispersions impede grain-boundary sliding.
Introducing stable nanoscale oxide particles during powder metallurgy produces an ODS tungsten variant with particles distributed at or near grain boundaries.
Oxide particles hinder dislocation climb during high-temperature deformation.
Hindering dislocation climb and grain-boundary sliding increases the energy required for plastic flow.
The oxide-mediated increase in resistance to plastic flow reduces the high-temperature plastic strain rate.
The oxide-mediated increase in resistance to plastic flow enhances tungsten toughness.
Under identical high-temperature loading, ODS tungsten will have a lower plastic strain rate than conventionally processed tungsten without a controlled oxide dispersion.
Under identical high-temperature loading, ODS tungsten will have greater fracture toughness or impact energy than conventionally processed tungsten without a controlled oxide dispersion.
The proposed effect should hold below tungsten's melting point when radiation damage is minimal or comparable between ODS and control specimens.
The long-term stability of nanoscale oxide dispersions under high-flux radiation has not been fully established.
